crater-lake-national-park.label: Protected by T.R.
crater-lake-national-park.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt signed the act creating it (1902-05-22).
crater-lake-national-park.note: A collapsed volcano holding the deepest lake in the United States. Roosevelt signed the bill creating the park on May 22, 1902.

wind-cave-national-park.label: Protected by T.R.
wind-cave-national-park.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt signed the act creating it (1903-01-09).
wind-cave-national-park.note: The first national park anywhere created to protect a cave. Roosevelt signed the act on January 9, 1903.

white-horse-hill-national-game-preserve.label: Protected by T.R.
white-horse-hill-national-game-preserve.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt signed the act creating Sully's Hill National Park (1904-06-02).
white-horse-hill-national-game-preserve.note: A wooded hill above Devils Lake, reserved by Roosevelt's proclamation of June 2, 1904. It became a game preserve in 1931 and, at the Spirit Lake Tribe's request, was renamed White Horse Hill National Game Preserve in 2019.

white-horse-hill-national-game-preserve.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
white-horse-hill-national-game-preserve.title: Partial Opening of Lands of the Sisseton, Wahpeton and Cut-Head Bands of the Sioux Indian Tribe
white-horse-hill-national-game-preserve.text: Proclamation 530 (1904-06-02): “Partial Opening of Lands of the Sisseton, Wahpeton and Cut-Head Bands of the Sioux Indian Tribe.” Today’s site began with this document.
white-horse-hill-national-game-preserve.note: Formerly Sully's Hill Park and then Sullys Hill National Game Preserve; renamed in 2019 at the Spirit Lake Tribe's request.

sources.name: Proclamation 530 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations

mesa-verde-national-park.label: Protected by T.R.
mesa-verde-national-park.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt signed the act creating it (1906-06-29).
mesa-verde-national-park.note: The first national park set aside to preserve the works of people: the cliff dwellings and mesa-top villages of the Ancestral Puebloans. Roosevelt signed the act on June 29, 1906.

chickasaw-national-recreation-area.label: Protected by T.R.
chickasaw-national-recreation-area.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt signed the act creating Platt National Park (1906-06-29).
chickasaw-national-recreation-area.note: Mineral and freshwater springs at Sulphur. Roosevelt signed the 1902 act creating the Sulphur Springs Reservation and the 1906 resolution renaming it Platt National Park. Since 1976 it has been part of Chickasaw National Recreation Area.

devils-tower-national-monument.label: Protected by T.R.
devils-tower-national-monument.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside it (1906-09-24).
devils-tower-national-monument.note: The first national monument, proclaimed under the brand-new Antiquities Act. The proclamation called the tower 'such an extraordinary example of the effect of erosion in the higher mountains as to be a natural wonder.'

devils-tower-national-monument.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
devils-tower-national-monument.title: Setting Aside Devils Tower National Monument, Wyoming
devils-tower-national-monument.text: Proclamation 658 (1906-09-24): “Setting Aside Devils Tower National Monument, Wyoming.” Today’s site began with this document.
devils-tower-national-monument.note: Now 1,347 acres, about 194 more than the 1,152.91 reserved in 1906.

sources.name: Proclamation 658 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations

el-morro-national-monument.label: Protected by T.R.
el-morro-national-monument.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside it (1906-12-08).
el-morro-national-monument.note: A sandstone bluff where centuries of travelers, from Ancestral Puebloans to Spanish and American passersby, carved their marks.

el-morro-national-monument.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
el-morro-national-monument.title: Setting Aside El Morro National Monument, New Mexico
el-morro-national-monument.text: Proclamation 695 (1906-12-08): “Setting Aside El Morro National Monument, New Mexico.” Today’s site began with this document.

montezuma-castle-national-monument.label: Protected by T.R.
montezuma-castle-national-monument.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside it (1906-12-08).
montezuma-castle-national-monument.note: A five-story Sinagua cliff dwelling tucked into a limestone cliff above Beaver Creek.

montezuma-castle-national-monument.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
montezuma-castle-national-monument.title: Setting Aside Montezuma Castle National Monument, Arizona
montezuma-castle-national-monument.text: Proclamation 696 (1906-12-08): “Setting Aside Montezuma Castle National Monument, Arizona.” Today’s site began with this document.
montezuma-castle-national-monument.note: 1,015.52 acres today, in two detached pieces: the Castle and Montezuma Well.

sources.name: Proclamation 696 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations
NPS Land Resources Division, listing of acreage, June 30, 2026

petrified-forest-national-park.label: Protected by T.R.
petrified-forest-national-park.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Petrified Forest National Monument (1906-12-08).
petrified-forest-national-park.note: Fallen logs from ancient forests, turned to stone and scattered across the painted desert. It became a national park in 1962.

petrified-forest-national-park.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
petrified-forest-national-park.title: Setting Aside Petrified Forest National Monument, Arizona
petrified-forest-national-park.text: Proclamation 697 (1906-12-08): “Setting Aside Petrified Forest National Monument, Arizona.” Today’s site absorbed into it.

NPS Land Resources Division, listing of acreage, June 30, 2026

chaco-culture-national-historical-park.label: Protected by T.R.
chaco-culture-national-historical-park.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Chaco Canyon National Monument (1907-03-11).
chaco-culture-national-historical-park.note: Great houses like Pueblo Bonito made this canyon the center of the Ancestral Puebloan world. Today it is Chaco Culture National Historical Park.

chaco-culture-national-historical-park.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
chaco-culture-national-historical-park.title: Setting Aside Chaco Canyon National Monument, New Mexico
chaco-culture-national-historical-park.text: Proclamation 740 (1907-03-11): “Setting Aside Chaco Canyon National Monument, New Mexico.” Today’s site absorbed into it.
chaco-culture-national-historical-park.note: The monument was abolished and the park established in its place in 1980; about 33,960 acres today.

lassen-volcanic-national-park.label: Protected by T.R.
lassen-volcanic-national-park.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Lassen Peak National Monument (1907-05-06).
lassen-volcanic-national-park.note: The volcano at the southern end of the Cascade Range. Its eruptions of 1914 to 1917 helped make it the heart of Lassen Volcanic National Park in 1916.

lassen-volcanic-national-park.label: Protected by T.R.
lassen-volcanic-national-park.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Cinder Cone National Monument (1907-05-06).
lassen-volcanic-national-park.note: A cone of volcanic cinders beside a lava field, Snag Lake and Lake Bidwell, set aside for what it shows about the region's volcanoes. Now part of Lassen Volcanic National Park.

lassen-volcanic-national-park.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
lassen-volcanic-national-park.title: Setting Aside Cinder Cone National Monument, California
lassen-volcanic-national-park.text: Proclamation 753 (1907-05-06): “Setting Aside Cinder Cone National Monument, California.” Today’s site absorbed into it.
lassen-volcanic-national-park.note: The 1916 park act drew its boundary around the monument without mentioning it.

sources.name: Proclamation 753 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations

lassen-volcanic-national-park.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
lassen-volcanic-national-park.title: Setting Aside Lassen Peak National Monument, California
lassen-volcanic-national-park.text: Proclamation 754 (1907-05-06): “Setting Aside Lassen Peak National Monument, California.” Today’s site absorbed into it.
lassen-volcanic-national-park.note: The park boundary takes in sections 34 and 35, where the monument lay.

sources.name: Proclamation 754 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations

gila-cliff-dwellings-national-monument.label: Protected by T.R.
gila-cliff-dwellings-national-monument.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside it (1907-11-16).
gila-cliff-dwellings-national-monument.note: Mogollon homes built into cliff caves above a fork of the Gila River. The proclamation called them 'the best representative of the Cliff-Dwellers' remains of that region.'

gila-cliff-dwellings-national-monument.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
gila-cliff-dwellings-national-monument.title: Establishment of the Gila Cliff-Dwellings National Monument, New Mexico
gila-cliff-dwellings-national-monument.text: Proclamation 781 (1907-11-16): “Establishment of the Gila Cliff-Dwellings National Monument, New Mexico.” Today’s site began with this document.
gila-cliff-dwellings-national-monument.note: Now 533 acres in two units; the only park system unit with Mogollon sites.

sources.name: Proclamation 781 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations

tonto-national-monument.label: Protected by T.R.
tonto-national-monument.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside it (1907-12-19).
tonto-national-monument.note: Salado cliff dwellings that today look out over Theodore Roosevelt Lake, the reservoir behind Roosevelt Dam.

tonto-national-monument.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
tonto-national-monument.title: Establishment of the Tonto National Monument, Arizona
tonto-national-monument.text: Proclamation 787 (1907-12-19): “Establishment of the Tonto National Monument, Arizona.” Today’s site began with this document.
tonto-national-monument.note: Now 1,120 acres: the original 640 plus 480 added in 1937.

sources.name: Proclamation 787 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations

muir-woods-national-monument.label: Protected by T.R.
muir-woods-national-monument.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside it (1908-01-09).
muir-woods-national-monument.note: Old-growth coast redwoods given to the nation by William and Elizabeth Thacher Kent, the first monument created on donated land. It was named for John Muir.

muir-woods-national-monument.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
muir-woods-national-monument.title: Setting Aside Muir Woods National Monument, California
muir-woods-national-monument.text: Proclamation 793 (1908-01-09): “Setting Aside Muir Woods National Monument, California.” Today’s site began with this document.
muir-woods-national-monument.note: The only old-growth coast redwood forest in the San Francisco Bay Area.

sources.name: Proclamation 793 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations

grand-canyon-national-park.label: Protected by T.R.
grand-canyon-national-park.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Grand Canyon National Monument (1908-01-11).

grand-canyon-national-park.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
grand-canyon-national-park.title: Setting Aside Game Preserve in Grand Canyon Forest Reserve, Arizona
grand-canyon-national-park.text: Proclamation 694 (1906-11-28): “Setting Aside Game Preserve in Grand Canyon Forest Reserve, Arizona.” Today’s site includes land from this document.
grand-canyon-national-park.note: The park took part of the preserve in 1919 and covers the plateau's southern end.

grand-canyon-national-park.title: Setting Aside Grand Canyon National Monument, Arizona
grand-canyon-national-park.text: Proclamation 794 (1908-01-11): “Setting Aside Grand Canyon National Monument, Arizona.” Today’s site absorbed into it.
grand-canyon-national-park.note: The 1919 act revoked the monument and folded its lands into the park; 4,919,163 recreation visits in 2024.

grand-canyon-national-park.title: Enlarging the Grand Canyon National Game Preserve, Arizona
grand-canyon-national-park.text: Proclamation 814 (1908-06-23): “Enlarging the Grand Canyon National Game Preserve, Arizona.” Today’s site includes land from this document.
grand-canyon-national-park.note: Much of the South Rim ground added in 1908 and kept in 1909 lies inside the park.

pinnacles-national-park.label: Protected by T.R.
pinnacles-national-park.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Pinnacles National Monument (1908-01-16).
pinnacles-national-park.note: Volcanic spires and talus caves in the Gabilan Mountains. It became Pinnacles National Park in 2013.

pinnacles-national-park.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
pinnacles-national-park.title: Setting Aside Pinnacles National Monument, California
pinnacles-national-park.text: Proclamation 796 (1908-01-16): “Setting Aside Pinnacles National Monument, California.” Today’s site began with this document.
pinnacles-national-park.note: About 26,700 acres today; redesignated a national park in 2013.

sources.name: Proclamation 796 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations

jewel-cave-national-monument.label: Protected by T.R.
jewel-cave-national-monument.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside it (1908-02-07).
jewel-cave-national-monument.note: A cave lined with sparkling calcite crystals in the Black Hills, now known to be one of the longest caves in the world.

jewel-cave-national-monument.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
jewel-cave-national-monument.title: Setting Aside Jewel Cave National Monument, South Dakota
jewel-cave-national-monument.text: Proclamation 799 (1908-02-07): “Setting Aside Jewel Cave National Monument, South Dakota.” Today’s site began with this document.
jewel-cave-national-monument.note: 1,273.51 acres, the Park Service's acreage of record.

natural-bridges-national-monument.label: Protected by T.R.
natural-bridges-national-monument.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside it (1908-04-16).
natural-bridges-national-monument.note: Three great stone bridges carved by White Canyon and its streams. Utah's first national monument.

natural-bridges-national-monument.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
natural-bridges-national-monument.title: Setting Aside Natural Bridges National Monument, Utah
natural-bridges-national-monument.text: Proclamation 804 (1908-04-16): “Setting Aside Natural Bridges National Monument, Utah.” Today’s site began with this document.
natural-bridges-national-monument.note: Utah's first national monument and the state's first unit of the national park system; about 7,636 acres today.

sources.name: Proclamation 804 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations
NPS Land Resources Division, listing of acreage, June 30, 2026

tumacacori-national-historical-park.label: Protected by T.R.
tumacacori-national-historical-park.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Tumacácori National Monument (1908-09-15).
tumacacori-national-historical-park.note: Ruins of a Spanish colonial mission church on the Santa Cruz River, now Tumacácori National Historical Park.

tumacacori-national-historical-park.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
tumacacori-national-historical-park.title: Setting Aside the Tumacacori National Monument, Arizona
tumacacori-national-historical-park.text: Proclamation 821 (1908-09-15): “Setting Aside the Tumacacori National Monument, Arizona.” Today’s site began with this document.
tumacacori-national-historical-park.note: The monument was abolished and the historical park created in its place in 1990.

sources.name: Proclamation 821 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations

wheeler-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Protected by T.R.
wheeler-national-wildlife-refuge.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Wheeler National Monument (1908-12-07).
wheeler-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Eroded spires of volcanic tuff high in the San Juan Mountains. Congress abolished the monument in 1950; it is now the Wheeler Geologic Area of Rio Grande National Forest.

wheeler-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
wheeler-national-wildlife-refuge.title: Setting Aside the Wheeler National Monument, Colorado
wheeler-national-wildlife-refuge.text: Proclamation 831 (1908-12-07): “Setting Aside the Wheeler National Monument, Colorado.” Today’s site no longer exists.
wheeler-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Abolished 1950; the formations are now the Wheeler Geologic Area of the Rio Grande National Forest, in the La Garita Wilderness.

sources.name: Proclamation 831 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations

olympic-national-park.label: Protected by T.R.
olympic-national-park.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Mount Olympus National Monument (1909-03-02).
olympic-national-park.note: Proclaimed two days before Roosevelt left office, to protect glaciers and the summer range of the Olympic elk, named Cervus roosevelti in his honor. It became Olympic National Park in 1938.

olympic-national-park.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
olympic-national-park.title: Setting Aside Mount Olympus National Monument, Washington
olympic-national-park.text: Proclamation 869 (1909-03-02): “Setting Aside Mount Olympus National Monument, Washington.” Today’s site absorbed into it.
olympic-national-park.note: Created in 1938 in place of the abolished monument; 922,650 acres today, home to the largest fully wild herd of Roosevelt elk in the Pacific Northwest.

pelican-island-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Protected by T.R.
pelican-island-national-wildlife-refuge.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Pelican Island Reservation (1903-03-14).
pelican-island-national-wildlife-refuge.note: A 5.5-acre island in the Indian River Lagoon became the first federal bird reservation, the seed of today's National Wildlife Refuge System. Roosevelt enlarged it on January 26, 1909.

pelican-island-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
pelican-island-national-wildlife-refuge.title: Pelican Island Reservation, Fla., established as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
pelican-island-national-wildlife-refuge.text: Unnumbered order (Lord no. 54) (1903-03-13): “Pelican Island Reservation, Fla., established as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds..” Today’s site began with this document.
pelican-island-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Renamed a national wildlife refuge in 1940.

sources.name: Unnumbered order (Lord no. 54) in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations

pelican-island-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
pelican-island-national-wildlife-refuge.title: Enlarging Pelican Island Reservation, Florida
pelican-island-national-wildlife-refuge.text: Executive Order 1014 (1909-01-26): “Enlarging Pelican Island Reservation, Florida.” Today’s site includes land from this document.
pelican-island-national-wildlife-refuge.note: The mangrove islands added in 1909 enlarged the first federal bird reservation.

sources.name: Executive Order 1014 in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations

breton-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Protected by T.R.
breton-national-wildlife-refuge.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Breton Island Reservation (1904-10-04).
breton-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Barrier islands off the Mississippi delta where terns and pelicans nest; Roosevelt came to see it for himself in 1915.

breton-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
breton-national-wildlife-refuge.title: Breton Island Reservation, St. Bernard and Plaquemines Parishes, La., established as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
breton-national-wildlife-refuge.text: Unnumbered order (Lord no. 98) (1904-10-04): “Breton Island Reservation, St. Bernard and Plaquemines Parishes, La., established as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds..” Today’s site began with this document.
breton-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Second-oldest refuge in the system; 1,100 acres in St. Bernard and Plaquemines parishes per the FWS fact sheet.

sources.name: Unnumbered order (Lord no. 98) in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations
U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service fact sheet

breton-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
breton-national-wildlife-refuge.title: Establishing Breton Island Reservation, Louisiana
breton-national-wildlife-refuge.text: Executive Order 369-A (1905-11-11): “Establishing Breton Island Reservation, Louisiana.” Today’s site includes land from this document.
breton-national-wildlife-refuge.note: The islands it covered remain part of the refuge.

sources.name: Executive Order 369-A in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations
EO 7983; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

stump-lake-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Protected by T.R.
stump-lake-national-wildlife-refuge.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Stump Lake Reservation (1905-03-09).
stump-lake-national-wildlife-refuge.note: North Dakota's first federal bird reservation: about 27 acres of islands in a prairie lake, still a refuge today.

stump-lake-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
stump-lake-national-wildlife-refuge.title: Creating Stump Lake Reservation, North Dakota, as Preserve and Breeding Ground for Birds
stump-lake-national-wildlife-refuge.text: Executive Order 296-A (1905-03-09): “Creating Stump Lake Reservation, North Dakota, as Preserve and Breeding Ground for Birds.” Today’s site began with this document.
stump-lake-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Administered from the Devils Lake Wetland Management District; closed to the public, its islands entirely under water.

huron-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Protected by T.R.
huron-national-wildlife-refuge.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Huron Islands Reservation (1905-10-10).
huron-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Rocky granite islands in Lake Superior where gulls nest, now also protected as wilderness.

huron-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
huron-national-wildlife-refuge.title: Establishing Huron Islands Reservation as a Preserve and Breeding Ground for Native Birds
huron-national-wildlife-refuge.text: Executive Order 357-D (1905-10-10): “Establishing Huron Islands Reservation as a Preserve and Breeding Ground for Native Birds.” Today’s site began with this document.
huron-national-wildlife-refuge.note: The 1905 order was revoked in 1938 and the refuge re-established under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act.

sources.name: Executive Order 357-D in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations
Executive Order 7795; Proclamation 2416; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

passage-key-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Protected by T.R.
passage-key-national-wildlife-refuge.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Passage Key Reservation (1905-10-10).
passage-key-national-wildlife-refuge.note: A shifting sand key at the mouth of Tampa Bay where seabirds and shorebirds nest.

passage-key-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
passage-key-national-wildlife-refuge.title: Establishing Passage Key Reservation as a Preserve and Breeding Ground for Native Birds
passage-key-national-wildlife-refuge.text: Executive Order 357-B (1905-10-10): “Establishing Passage Key Reservation as a Preserve and Breeding Ground for Native Birds.” Today’s site began with this document.
passage-key-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Renamed a national wildlife refuge in 1940; now a small sandbar closed to the public.

sources.name: Executive Order 357-B in Theodore Roosevelt’s Executive Orders and Proclamations
Proclamation 2416; U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

shell-keys-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Protected by T.R.
shell-keys-national-wildlife-refuge.text: As President, Theodore Roosevelt set aside Shell Keys Reservation (1907-08-17).
shell-keys-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Tiny shell islands in the Gulf south of Marsh Island, among the smallest refuges in the system.

midway-atoll-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order
midway-atoll-national-wildlife-refuge.title: Placing the Midway Islands Under the Jurisdiction and Control of the Navy Department
midway-atoll-national-wildlife-refuge.text: Executive Order 199-A (1903-01-20): “Placing the Midway Islands Under the Jurisdiction and Control of the Navy Department.” Today’s site transferred to it.
midway-atoll-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Navy control that began with this order ended in 1996, when Executive Order 13022 transferred the atoll to the Interior Department for the refuge.

pinellas-national-wildlife-refuge.label: Traces to a T.R. proclamation or order

pinellas-national-wildlife-refuge.text: Executive Order 409 (1906-02-10): “Establishing Indian Key Reservation, Tampa Bay, Florida as Preserve and Breeding Ground for Birds.” Today’s site includes land from this document.
pinellas-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Established in 1951; takes in Indian, Tarpon, Mule and Jackass Keys, closed to the public, managed within the Crystal River refuge complex.

san-juan-islands-national-wildlife-refug.note: Viti Rocks, off the south end of Lummi Island, are now part of the refuge.
